messages.subject: Re: still having problems adding unique vertical lines to facets of density plots and histograms
parts:
On 7/27/2012 5:09 PM, Tarek Elnaccash wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I'm very new to R and ggplot2 and I'm stuck on a problem I've seen several
> people post about already. I am trying to add unique vertical lines to
> each facet of a multi-paneled set of density plots. I have read advice on
> several sites saying that I need to make a dataframe with the xintercepts
> and the facet levels. When i tried this, I was able to get my plots and
> vertical lines, but every line is matched to every plot instead of two
> lines per plot. Since this is my first time using ggplot2, I dont know if
> I have just made a typo or if I misunderstand the correct syntax. More
> details of my problem are listed below. I have also attached the plot I
> created with my last line of code below. How can I put the correct unique
> lines on each plot?
>
> thanks in advance!
>
> Tarek Elnaccash
>
>
> I have a dataframe with a continuous variable (totg) and a categorical
> variable (nlvls) and I am trying to use ggplot2 to make 4 vertically
> stacked density plots, with different vertical lines marked of on each
> histogram. This code worked without creating any vertical lines:
>
> ggplot(data=nexpt, aes(totg) ) + geom_density() + facet_grid(nlvl ~ . )
>
> I read that I have to create a dataframe to make different vertical lines
> for each facet, which I did like this:
>
> vline.totg.cvi<-data.frame(z=levels(nexpt$nlvl), vl=c(
> nexpt[481, 3 ],
> nexpt[321, 3 ],
> nexpt[161, 3 ],
> nexpt[1, 3 ]
>
> ))
> vline.totg.ler<-data.frame(z=levels(nexpt$nlvl), vl=c(
> nexpt[482, 3 ],
> nexpt[322, 3 ],
> nexpt[162, 3 ],
> nexpt[2, 3 ]
> ))

Here is your problem. Faceting is done based on the variable nlvl, but
there is no nlvl in these data frames. Rather, you have named it z.
Change the name to nlvl and it should work.

vline.totg.cvi<-data.frame(nlvl=levels(nexpt$nlvl), vl=c(
nexpt[481, 3 ],
nexpt[321, 3 ],
nexpt[161, 3 ],
nexpt[1, 3 ]
))
vline.totg.ler<-data.frame(nlvl=levels(nexpt$nlvl), vl=c(
nexpt[482, 3 ],
nexpt[322, 3 ],
nexpt[162, 3 ],
nexpt[2, 3 ]
))


> which produced the following data frames:
>
> > vline.totg.cvi
>
> z vl
> 1 N01 0.07931
> 2 N06 0.21393
> 3 N51 0.94026
> 4 N56 1.29206
>
> > vline.totg.ler
>
> z vl
> 1 N01 0.02638
> 2 N06 0.11094
> 3 N51 0.76690
> 4 N56 0.27937
>
> When I tried this ggplot2 code to put vertical lines on my density plots,
> it put all the lines on all plots instead of one blue line (and one green)
> on each plot:
>
> ggplot(data=nexpt, aes(totg) ) + geom_density() +
> geom_vline(aes(xintercept=vl), data=vline.totg.cvi,colour="blue") +
> facet_grid(nlvl ~ . )
>
> AND
>
> ggplot(data=nexpt, aes(totg) ) + geom_density() +
> geom_vline(aes(xintercept=vl), data=vline.totg.cvi,colour="blue") +
> facet_grid(nlvl ~ . ) + geom_vline(aes(xintercept=vl),
> data=vline.totg.ler,colour="green")
>
> How can I correct this??
>
> -Tarek
>
>
>> levels(nexpt$nlvl)
> [1] "N01" "N06" "N51" "N56"
>> summary(nexpt$totg)
> Min. 1st Qu. Median Mean 3rd Qu. Max. NA's
> -0.03451 0.08994 0.30080 0.51720 0.75220 3.21800 13
>
>> sessionInfo()
> R version 2.15.0 (2012-03-30)
> Platform: x86_64-pc-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
>
> locale:
> [1] LC_COLLATE=English_United States.1252 LC_CTYPE=English_United
> States.1252
> [3] LC_MONETARY=English_United States.1252 LC_NUMERIC=C
>
> [5] LC_TIME=English_United States.1252
>
> attached base packages:
> [1] grid stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods
> base
>
